question: The government of India decided that Medium-term and Long-Term Government Deposit (MLTGD) components of Gold Monetisation Scheme (GMS) shall be discontinued from:
solution:
The correct answer is __**26 March 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The government of India decided to discontinue the Medium-term and Long-term Government Deposit (MLTGD) components of the Gold Monetisation Scheme (GMS) from **26 March 2025**.
 
• The Gold Monetisation Scheme (GMS) was introduced in **2015** to mobilize idle gold and put it into productive use in the economy.
 
• MLTGD components under GMS allowed individuals and institutions to deposit gold for medium-term (5-7 years) and long-term (12-15 years) tenure.
 
• Discontinuing MLTGD components aligns with the government's strategy to streamline the gold monetisation process and focus on other viable components like short-term deposits.
 
• Depositors under the GMS were offered **interest rates** on their gold deposits, encouraging participation in the scheme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gold Monetisation Scheme (GMS):**

 
 
• Launched by the Government of India in **November 2015** to reduce the dependency on gold imports and utilize idle gold reserves.
 
• Allows individuals and institutions to deposit gold in exchange for interest and withdrawal options.
 
• Gold deposits under GMS are accepted by banks and refineries for further utilization.
 
 
 
• **Medium-term and Long-term Government Deposits (MLTGD):**
 
 
• MLTGD components involve depositing gold for periods of 5-7 years (medium-term) and 12-15 years (long-term).
 
• These deposits were aimed at institutional investors and individuals seeking higher returns over extended durations.
 
 
 
• **Short-term Gold Deposit:**
 
 
• Short-term deposits under GMS are typically for a tenure of 1-3 years.
 
• These deposits are primarily used by banks for internal purposes like reserve management.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of GMS:**
 
 
• To mobilize idle gold lying with households and institutions in India.
 
• To reduce reliance on gold imports, which contribute significantly to India's trade deficit.
 
• To provide benefits to depositors in the form of interest on their gold holdings.
